Karel Čapek, The Absolute at Large, translated by Šárka B. Hrbková.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/karel-capek/the-absolute-at-large/sarka-b-hrbkova

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Karel Čapek, the author, died 1938 (Wikidata Q155855, P570 = 1938-12-25).
- Šárka B. Hrbková, the translator, died 1948 (Wikidata Q84169049, P570 = 1948-00-00 and 1948-02-07; both dates are in 1948).

First publication of the text used: 1927 (SE colophon: 'The Absolute at Large was published in 1922 by Karel Čapek. It was translated from Czech in 1927 by Šárka B. Hrbková.'). The country of this translation's first publication is not stated in the facts.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1927, before 1931, so the United States public domain applies to it.
- Country of origin: the last person to die, Šárka B. Hrbková, died in 1948. The original Czech work was first published in 1922 in Czechoslovakia, where Karel Čapek's term is life + 70 years and the work entered the public domain on 1 January 2009. The possible countries for the English translation (the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa) each have a term of life + 70 years or less, and the text is public domain in each of them since 2019.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
